haiku-low.q1: They see the generic reply: HTTP 200, "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is stored or sent.
haiku-low.q2: The fourth request is refused with the generic reply. No row is created, no email is queued, and the earlier link stays unchanged.
haiku-low.q3: A link lasts 30 minutes from issue. It ends sooner if it is used, or killed when a newer link is issued for the same account.
haiku-low.q4: The link stays live and unused, so the user can try again until it expires. Rejected passwords never consume the link.
haiku-low.q5: None. All sessions are deleted in the same transaction, no session is created, and the user is redirected to /login to log in again.
haiku-low.q6: The worker retries 3 times with backoff, then logs and drops the job. Nobody is notified, and the user sees nothing.
haiku-low.q7: The raw token is put into the link, which is sent in the queued job. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored in the database.
haiku-low.q8: It hashes the token from the URL and finds the row by token_hash. It checks used_at and killed_at are NULL and that now() is before expires_at.
haiku-low.q9: Not in a separate counter. It counts password_resets rows for that user issued in the last hour; older rows fall outside that window.
haiku-low.q10: Older live links get killed_at set to now() in the same transaction that inserts the new link row, before commit.
haiku-low.q11: The password hash update, marking the link used, and deleting sessions commit together. The "password changed" email is queued after that commit.
haiku-low.q12: The conditional UPDATE of used_at only matches while the link is live, so one submit changes the row and the other changes zero rows and gets "link expired".

sonnet.q1: They see the generic reply (HTTP 200, "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link."). Nothing is stored or sent.
sonnet.q2: Count of links in last hour is already >= 3, so rollback: no row, no job, earlier link unchanged. They get the same generic reply.
sonnet.q3: 30 minutes from issue (expires_at = issued_at + 30m). Sooner: being used (used_at set) or killed by a newer link for the same account.
sonnet.q4: Untouched and still live (until it expires). The form is re-shown with an error.
sonnet.q5: None: all sessions for the user are deleted (all devices logged out, effective on their next request). The user is redirected (302) to /login and logs in with the new password; no session is created by the reset.
sonnet.q6: The worker retries 3 times with backoff, then logs and drops the job. The user is not told; nobody is notified. They may request again (counts toward 3 per hour).
sonnet.q7: The raw token is generated at request time, put into the link in the queued job {address, link}, and the worker sends that email. Only the hash is stored in the DB. (The document does not give further mechanics.)
sonnet.q8: The server hashes the token T, finds the password_resets row by token_hash, and checks it is live: used_at IS NULL, killed_at IS NULL and now() < expires_at. Unknown, expired, used or killed shows the expired page.
sonnet.q9: NOT STATED as a stored counter: there is no separate counter. It is computed by counting password_resets rows for the user, in any state, issued in the last hour. Old requests drop out as their issued_at passes one hour; rows may also be deleted by optional housekeeping after a day.
sonnet.q10: Older live links are killed (killed_at = now()) in step 5 of the request flow, in the same transaction that inserts the new row, before COMMIT. The user row is locked (FOR UPDATE) beforehand.
sonnet.q11: In one transaction: the link's used_at is set, the user's password hash is updated, and all the user's sessions are deleted; then COMMIT. The "password changed" email job is queued after the commit (step 6), not part of the transaction.
sonnet.q12: A conditional UPDATE sets used_at = now() WHERE id = row.id AND the link is live. Only one gets a changed row; the other gets 0 rows, rolls back and sees the "link expired" page.
